messages:
Priya: Heads-up — AcmeCorp reported a big p99 spike after we onboarded gnome-v1 yesterday. They see tail latency go from ~450ms -> 2.4s for long inputs (>2048 tokens). Raised to support at 09:12 PT.
Marco: Ack, can you paste the example request + any logs?
Priya: Here's the curl they used (redacted API key):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gnome-v1","input":"<~3k chars long prompt>","max_tokens":512}'
```
Priya: Observed pattern: short requests ok, long-context requests p95 up slightly but p99 blows up. Customer timeline shows spike starting right after we flipped model/tokenizer variant.
Lin: We merged the tokenizer subword merge (PR #4821) as part of gnome-v1 onboarding. That changed some UTF-8 normalization and subtoken boundaries; could cause token inflation for certain corpora.
Dana: From infra metrics: batcher latency increases at queue size thresholds when per-request token count jumps. I see KV-cache miss rate increase for sessions >2048 tokens (kv_cache_miss % jumped 3x).
Marco: Runtime traces show extra time in `tokenize()` path for ~30% of long requests — CPU-bound operation before dispatch to GPU. Looks like we moved some normalization from C++ path to Python layer in the tokenizer change.
Priya: Customer provided a sample long input that reproduces locally. I ran a repro in sandbox and saw the same p99 tail. Log snippet: `tokenize_time=0.82s total_latency=2.12s gpu_time=0.45s`.
Marco: That matches: tokenize_time dominating. Can we get a small repro vector? Priya: Pasted in thread DMed, shared via secure link.
Lin: Quick hypothesis: new tokenizer does extra normalization and produces 10-30% more subtokens for some unicode-heavy inputs -> extra KV cache lookups and batcher pressure. Also possible we're triggering a slow fallback in the tokenizer for rare codepoints.
Dana: Mitigation options I can do quickly: 1) Route AcmeCorp requests to gnome-v1-tokenizer-legacy variant (old tokenizer) as a customer-scoped fallback; 2) Increase batcher window & temporary extra shards for the model to avoid head-of-line blocking; 3) Warm KV cache / pinning for active sessions.
Priya: Customer agreed to a temporary routing change. Can we do (1) as hotpatch?
Marco: I'll prepare a runtime route rule to prefer `gnome-v1+legacy-tokenizer` for that org. Should be a config flip. Dana, can you increase shards by one in prod pool for gnome-v1 for the next 6 hours?
Dana: On it. Pushing a rollback-safe change: add route, scale +1 shard, and bump batcher timeout from 20ms -> 30ms for gnome-v1. Deploying now.
ops-bot: Deploy started by Dana: deploy/infra/2026-03-17-hotpatch-gnome-token-route (sha: a1b2c3)
Priya: After routing, AcmeCorp reports p99 dropped from 2.4s -> 520ms within 8 minutes. They validated a few failing prompts. :white_check_mark:
Lin: I'll revert the tokenizer normalization change in the tokenizer branch and create a new PR with a micro-optimization — move expensive normalization back to C++ layer where possible. Target: PR by end of day, can be staged to canary.
Marco: Also adding a guard in runtime: if tokenize_time > 200ms for a request, we mark it for async tokenization + early dispatch to GPU with placeholder KV handling (experimental). Filing issue #6002.
Dana: Scaling & route changes will stay until we've validated PR in canary and run 24h perf. Rolling metrics to track: p95/p99, tokenize_time histogram, kv_cache_miss, batcher_queue_size.
Priya: Owners: Lin -> tokenizer PR + repro tests; Marco -> runtime guard + traces; Dana -> hotpatch rollback plan + metrics dashboard. I will own customer comms.
Marco: Quick note for postmortem: include prompt corpus stats that triggered most inflation and add tests in onboarding checklist to run a long-context tokenization diff against baseline variant.
Lin: I already added a `tokenize-diff` unit that compares token count distribution vs baseline for 1k sample prompts. Will expand to the onboarding pipeline.
Priya: Closing loop: customer satisfied with temporary fix, will keep monitoring. ETA for full fix: 48 hours (tokenizer PR + canary validation).
Dana: Deploy finished. All hotpatch changes logged in infra audit. ops-bot will mark incident as monitored.
ops-bot: Deploy finished by Dana: deploy/infra/2026-03-17-hotpatch-gnome-token-route (status: success)
Priya: Adding short repro steps to thread for SRE runbook: 1) send sample long prompt 2) check `tokenize_time` & `kv_cache_miss` 3) if p99 > 1.5s route to legacy-tokenizer variant 4) escalate to Lin/Marco/Dana.
Marco: Thanks — I'll add a short alert to trigger at tokenize_time > 300ms for a model to auto-notify eng-runtime.
Priya: 👍 Thanks team. Will update AcmeCorp and tag this for postmortem notes.
